posts.title: Passenger Spine: Travel Between Districts
posts.summary: Passenger trams, lifts, and pedestrian connectors serve the Hub's main districts. Ordinary passenger service is free.
body: Freight traffic uses separate industrial routes. Public passenger access does not authorize entry into controlled work areas.
A work credential may establish eligibility for specific duties or facilities, but it is not a universal access pass.

posts.title: Who Handles a Held Cargo Release?
posts.summary: An active cargo hold may require separate handling, commercial, guarantee, and claims decisions. One desk cannot clear every restriction.
body: Dock Labor Assembly handles work-floor safety and labor access. Ledger Quay handles commercial manifests, release recognition, and bonded procedure.
Bonded Freight Brokers may handle guarantees. The Hub Claims Registry handles relevant disputes over title, custody, liens, and identity. The responsible office depends on the specific issue.

comments.text: Ask which hold is actually in force before getting bounced between counters.
An authorized release on paper still isn't permission to work the floor.

posts.title: Where Do You Hear News Before It Reaches a Terminal?
posts.summary: Residents discuss the mix of district notices, workplace briefings, visiting crews, and word of mouth.
body: Local information moves through many channels. A claim can circulate widely without being corroborated. A public terminal entry is not proof that everyone on the Hub has seen it.

comments.text: Work briefings are good for what's happening on your own shift. Not much else.
Word of mouth gets there first. Getting the details right is another matter.
